academic_translation: Herein is contained the Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter.
translation: Here is the noble perfect wisdom called the Diamond Cutter.

academic_translation: In the language of India: Ārya Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra.
translation: In the language of India: Diamond Cutter.

academic_translation: In the Tibetan language: The Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Mahāyāna sūtra.
translation: In the Tibetan language: The noble perfect wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Great Vehicle sacred text.

academic_translation: Homage to all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
translation: I bow to all Buddhas and awakening heroes.

academic_translation: Thus did I hear at one time.
translation: This is what I heard one time.

academic_translation: The Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī at Jetavana, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks, and very many bodhisattva great beings.
translation: The Blessed One was staying in Shravasti at the Jeta Grove, the park of Anathapindada. A great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks was there. Many great awakening heroes were with him too.

academic_translation: Then, in the morning time, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and Dharma robe, took up his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
translation: In the morning, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and his teaching robe. He picked up his alms bowl. He walked into the great city of Shravasti for his alms food.

academic_translation: Then the Blessed One, having gone to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms, partook of his meal and completed the action of eating,
translation: The Blessed One went to the great city of Shravasti for alms food. He ate his meal and finished eating.

academic_translation: Having given up the alms of the later meal, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robe, washed his feet, sat cross-legged on the arranged seat, straightened his body, and remained, having established mindfulness to the fore.
translation: He finished eating his alms food. He put away his alms bowl and teaching robe. He washed his feet and sat cross-legged on his seat. He sat up straight with careful attention, ready to pay full attention.

academic_translation: Then many monks went to where the Blessed One was, and having approached him,
translation: Then many monks went over to where the Blessed One was. They walked right up to him.

academic_translation: They bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side.
translation: They bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One. They walked around him three times and sat down to one side.

academic_translation: Also at that time, the venerable Subhūti had assembled in that very assembly and was seated there.
translation: At that time, the honored Subhuti was also sitting there in the assembly.

academic_translation: Then the venerable Subhūti rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right kneecap on the ground, and bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One.
translation: Then the honored Subhuti stood up from his seat. He put his upper robe over one shoulder. He put his right knee on the ground. He put his palms together and bowed to the Blessed One.

academic_translation: He addressed the Blessed One with these words:
translation: He spoke these words to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, it is wonderful to what supreme extent the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and to what supreme extent the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!
translation: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha, has helped the great awakening heroes in the highest way. It is wonderful how the Thus-Gone One has placed the highest trust in the great awakening heroes. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Well-Gone One, it is wonderful!"

academic_translation: Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
translation: "Blessed One, how should someone who has entered the awakening hero's vehicle live?"

academic_translation: How should one practice?
translation: "How should they practice?"

academic_translation: How should one hold the mind?
translation: "How should they keep the mind steady?"

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus,
translation: When he had said this,

academic_translation: The Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: The Blessed One said this to the honored Subhuti:

academic_translation: Subhūti, excellent, excellent!
translation: Subhuti, excellent, excellent!

academic_translation: Subhūti, it is so, it is so.
translation: Subhuti, it is so, it is so.

academic_translation: The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme benefit.
translation: The Thus-Gone One has given the greatest help to the great awakening heroes.

academic_translation: The Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme entrustment.
translation: The Thus-Gone One has given the greatest trust to the great awakening heroes.

academic_translation: Therefore, Subhūti, listen, attend properly, and hold it thoroughly in mind, and
translation: Therefore, Subhuti, listen carefully, pay close attention, and keep this in mind.

academic_translation: I shall explain to you how one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should abide, how one should practice, and how one should hold the mind.
translation: I will explain how someone who has correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should live, how they should practice, and how they should keep the mind steady.

academic_translation: Having replied, "Blessed One, it is so,"
translation: He answered, "Blessed One, it is so."

academic_translation: the venerable Subhūti listened to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: The honored Subhuti listened to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One spoke these words to the honored Subhuti:

tibetan: རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པས། འདི་སྙམ་དུ་བདག་གིས་སེམས་ཅན་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བསྡུ་བས་བསྡུས་པ། སྒོ་ང་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། མངལ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། དྲོད་གཤེར་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། རྫུས་ཏེ་སྐྱེས་པའམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་ནམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་མ་ཡིན་པའམ། འདུ་ཤེས་ཅན་ནམ། འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་མིན་ནམ། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་གདགས་པའི་བརྟགས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་དབྱིངས་སུ་ཡོངས་སུ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདའོ། །
academic_translation: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: 'However many sentient beings are subsumed by the subsumption of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, or born from a womb, or born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born, or having form, or without form, or having perception, or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings, all those I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'

locked_terms.use: neither with ideas nor without ideas
expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over

translation: Subhuti, someone who has correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should think like this: 'I must help all kinds of living beings. This includes those born from eggs, or born from a womb. It includes those born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born. It includes those having a shape, and those without form. It includes those having ideas, and those without ideas. It even includes those neither with ideas nor without ideas. However many exist in the realm of living beings, I will lead them all to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.'

academic_translation: Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.
translation: Countless living beings are led to complete freedom from sorrow in this way. But you must set the mind to think that no living being at all has been led to complete freedom from sorrow.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because they would not be called a bodhisattva.
translation: Why is that? Because then they would not be called an awakening hero.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because, Subhūti, if one engages in the perception of a sentient being, engages in the perception of a life-force, or engages in the perception of a person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva.
translation: Why is that? Because, Subhuti, if someone has the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, or the idea of a person, they are not called an awakening hero.

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in an entity.
translation: Also, Subhuti, an awakening hero should practice giving without staying in a real object.

academic_translation: They should practice generosity without abiding in anything.
translation: They should practice giving without staying in anything.

academic_translation: They should practice generosity without abiding in form.
translation: They should practice giving without staying in a shape.

academic_translation: Likewise, generosity should be practiced without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, or even phenomena.
translation: In the same way, they should practice giving without staying in a sound, a smell, a taste, a thing that is touched, or even a thing.

academic_translation: Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity in such a way that they are without abiding even in the perception of a sign.
translation: Subhuti, an awakening hero should practice giving without staying even in the idea of a sign.

academic_translation: Why is that?
translation: Why is that?

academic_translation: Subhūti, it is because the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding is not easy to measure, Subhūti.
translation: Subhuti, it is because when an awakening hero practices giving without staying, their pile of stored-up goodness is not easy to measure, Subhuti.

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think it is easy to measure space in the eastern direction?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think? Is it easy to measure space in the east?
